What if Elon Musk's companies aren't separate businesses at all... but parts of one giant machine?
Start with the brain: an AI called Grok, built by xAI.
A brain needs to learn. So it trains on Colossus, a supercomputer xAI says it built in just 122 days.
Learning needs data. X adds a stream of posts every second.
Millions of Teslas add something rarer: video of real roads.
And Optimus, the humanoid robot, could one day learn from the physical world itself.
But every AI hits the same wall. It's hungry. For chips. For power. For cooling.
Musk has even floated building his own giant chip factory.
Tesla Energy already sells solar panels and giant batteries.
And SpaceX has the rockets... plus Starlink, thousands of satellites wrapping the planet in internet.
In space, sunlight never stops, and the cold is free. Musk has talked about putting AI computers into orbit, powered by the Sun.
Rockets carry the computers. Starlink connects them. The Sun feeds them.
And the last piece? Neuralink, a chip that connects a human brain to a computer.
So is it a business empire... or one machine, being assembled piece by piece?
